motivo: Claim that 127-kyr paleosol DNA records ancient communities needs 291-bp (16S amplicon) and 457-bp (qPCR) templates to survive 24-127 kyr at ~14-19 C. With Allentoft-type decay rates unprotected survival fails in 100% of draws; it only works with an unquantified ~14-113x (5-95%: 5-322x) mineral/dryness protection factor or with dormant cells intact for 1e4-1e5 yr, which the paper assumes but does not justify (high-MW DNA on gels points to living present-day cells).

Table 2 "Modern C (%)" reproduces exactly as 100xTOC(wt%)xf, i.e. modern C per unit of ROCK, yet is reported as 0.46-2.36% of the TOC pool. By the paper's own Eq. 1 the modern fraction of TOC is (D14C+1000)/1000 = 2.3-23% (1.5-14% with a +600 permil endmember): error factor = 1/TOC = 3.3-71 in all 10 samples, so the "small" input in the title is understated. DOC infiltration would also need ~4500 yr (5-95%: 435-5e4 yr) to deliver that stock, inconsistent with a ~0 permil modern endmember in 97% of draws. No published correction found.

The interface migration of 0.40 um/s at 1200 C matches C-diffusion-controlled decarburization (D_C,austenite ~1.3e-10 m2/s gives v = lam*sqrt(D/t) of 0.26 um/s, 5-95% 0.08-0.55; ratio median 1.5, P(>=3)=0.18). Error noted: Eq. 3 (dL proportional to Dt) is dimensionally wrong, since diffusion gives sqrt(Dt), and 4 points over 1070-1460 s cannot tell linear from parabolic growth.

An Mw 5.9 event can trigger liquefaction out to about 17 km (Ambraseys 1988), so a Jishishan-like quake 4 km from Lajia is feasible. But the 2023 cascade (675,000 m3 deposit, ~3.7 m thick) depended on irrigation-saturated loess with a frozen crust, which the paper itself calls "the culprit". It never states or justifies equivalent saturation at 4000 BP, and the Lajia match is only by sediment composition.

Claims village abandonment follows demographic stochasticity (random births/deaths/migration). A linear birth-death model run on the authors' own village populations (1596 median 145, 1881 median 200), with households treated as units, predicts 1881-1931 abandonment of 0.46% (95th pct 1.4%) vs 17.1% observed: ratio >=3 in 100% of draws. For 1596-1881 it predicts 8% vs 42.5% observed (ratio >=3 in 67%). The observed turnover needs correlated, causal processes.

Lake dimensions not given (assumed 2-10 ha, 3-6 m mean depth). Removing hypolimnetic O2 (~0.9 t) would need only ~6 t of straw per season (5-95%: 2-16 t), about 1.7 ha of hemp, which is plausible for a nearby settlement. So retting-driven allochthonous loading and anoxia are physically feasible.

The stated mechanism ("supersaturation of the colloidal metal-glass system" leading to agglomeration) would need ~1e10 yr of Brownian coagulation in a 30-3000 Pa s melt to grow nm particles into 6-10 mm spheres: ratio to furnace time ~1e13, >=3 in 100% of draws. Only coarse undissolved scrap (0.1-1 mm) settling by Stokes law (~12 h median) is feasible, consistent with the CT-visible fragments, but that is not the colloidal process the paper concludes.

Ratio median 24, >=3 in 93% of draws (100% with human-physiology BAT priors), so BAT cannot be the explanation.

Solution kinetics (Gln t1/2 6100 d at 37 C) scaled to 8-20 C give ~270-yr Gln and ~3-yr Asn half-times, so near-complete deamidation is expected after 500-8000 yr. The observed partial and highly variable ancient deamidation implies matrix-slowed kinetics or mixtures, consistent with the paper's cautious conclusion that deamidation alone cannot authenticate.

Matching oxo-BA/BA ratios to modern faeces after ~1945 yr requires differential degradation below 1.3e-4/yr (differential half-life >5000 yr for <=30% drift). The paper itself says BAs are less stable than oxo-BAs, and no degradation rates are given or available in standard sources.

Ranking (patina+fresh coating best, bronze disease worst) is robust, but the absolute rates are not. BD icorr of 582 uA/cm2 (6.76 mm/yr) is 7.7x the O2 diffusion limit in quiescent NaCl (~76 uA/cm2; >=3 in 99.6% of draws), so it holds only if an unstated extra cathodic reaction (reduction of CuCl/atacamite corrosion products) operates. Arithmetic errors: CR not proportional to icorr for S1-S3 (x1.3-2.0); E% computed from CR, not Eq. 1 (S1 50.6 vs 62.9, S2 64.6 vs 82.3); Rp(S3) 6921 vs Stern-Geary 4743.

Microbe removal "because of 3-4 A molecular-sieve pores" fails by a size ratio of ~1250-6700 (bacteria 0.5-2 um). An ingress filter of 5-100 m2 facing storm inflows of ~3100 m3/h (5-95%: 740-12,700) would need ~600x more area at pathogen-removing loading rates (>=3 in 100% of draws), and ~15x even at rapid-filter rates (>=3 in 89%). The paper also says the 0.1-10 um zeolite was readily washed out. Mineral presence does not support a functioning purification system.
